evidence.location: §2 VG4, first-document bullet; §3 VG4 homes row
evidence.observation: The plan says "The test is read on the root's own document, as authored, before composition merges the included elements into it" and "It cannot be read on the composed document". The VG4 homes list "`src/gnd/model/__init__.py` (the root's own document reaches U1)". The shipped code does the opposite. src/gnd/model/_unattended.py:293-299 defines `_owns_nothing`, whose docstring says "Read on the composed document with VG3's origin set". The phase-VG4-spec §4 says "Whether the composed reading equals the root's own file is measured by T3's per-section cases". The 005-phase-VG4.md 'What shipped' list names no change to model/__init__.py. §11 has no amendment for either sentence.

evidence.location: 'Spec-level changes recorded in the phases', VG4 bullet
evidence.observation: The VG4 bullet lists only "the first-document add creates the list only on an unattended model; a present `documents: null` keeps U1; T5 does not compare against a flattened copy". It does not mention that U1's test moved from the authored root to the composed document plus _INCLUDED. With that move, U1 is correct only when the context variable is set, and VG3 sets it "only by `_model_warnings`".

The row reads "the spec-level open questions of plan §10 (VG1 table home, VG3 origin route and line text, VG4 D6 home) | closed by VG1-D1, VG3-D1, VG3-D2, VG4-D2". Plan §10 also carried "VG4, how the root's own document reaches U1". That question is not listed here and is not dispositioned anywhere in the results.

concerns.recommendation: Add the change to close-delta's VG4 bullet: U1's first-document test reads the composed document with VG3's origin set, and VG4-C3/T3 measure its equivalence to the authored root. Add a §11 amendment that keeps the §2 sentence and the §3 `model/__init__.py` home and states what shipped. Add the missing §10 question to the results row and close it by the VG4 spec's U1 section.
concerns.title: VG4 moved U1's first-document test to the composed document, against the plan text, and no close artifact records it

evidence.observation: The row says "`ModelIndex`'s cache key admits two models whose values differ; readers other than the VG1 tables still read the first model's rows". This implies the VG1 tables are always safe. The 002-phase-VG1.md Boundary section says otherwise: "Past the routed reader's 10 MB or 64-level caps the tables read the cached rows, so the F1 collision can still reach a model that large." The code agrees: src/gnd/model_index.py:304-307 falls back to `return self._document` with the comment "Over the routed reader's 10 MB or 64-level caps: the cached rows, as before VG1 (a residual the VG1 record names)".

Amendment 5 says "the tables live on `ModelIndex` and are built from the canonical JSON form the cache key is a digest of, not from the cached rows" and gives no exception. close-delta.md item 5 repeats it: "VG1's tables are built from the canonical JSON form ... not from the cached rows".

concerns.recommendation: In the results row, the delta item and §11 amendment 5, say that VG1's tables also read the cached rows past the routed reader's 10 MB or 64-level caps. Carry that cap case under the same maintenance-pass disposition as the cache-key question.
concerns.title: The results row and amendment 5 omit the VG1 tables' size-cap fallback to cached rows

summary: Every goal predicate cites a test from its phase record, and I checked those records (002–006) against the predicates. I read the U1 first-document code in _unattended.py and the VG1 tables in model_index.py; both behave as the records say, and a model without the mode or without includes is unchanged. I found nothing blocking. Two consistency gaps remain. First, VG4 reads the first-document test on the composed document. Plan §2 and §3 say this cannot be done, and neither the close delta, the §11 amendments nor the open-question row records the change. Second, the results row on the cache key and amendment 5 leave out the size-cap residual that the VG1 record and the code both name.
